notes.subject: קדשה/קדש
notes.rationale: Both words come from the root קדש (holi) — 'consecrated one', used here for a cultic prostitute; the irony of the holy root is lost in Tok Pisin.

notes.subject: קדשה
notes.rationale: Cultic shrine-prostitute (root 'holy') vs ordinary harlot — 'salim bodi long nem bilong ol god' keeps the cultic sense against KJV 'whore'.

notes.subject: olsem
notes.rationale: Second clause abbreviates; 'olsem' (likewise) supplied to carry the repeated verb, marked ⟨…⟩ where not in Hebrew.

translation: Ol pikinini meri bilong Yisrael i no ken kamap ⟨ol⟩ meri i salim bodi long nem bilong ol god, na ol pikinini man bilong Yisrael i no ken kamap olsem.
